---
title: "Tutorial: a price-triggered lock"
description: Build a lock that releases funds once BTC/USDT crosses a price, and run it on testnet.
---

This tutorial follows the reference consumer in the repository:
[`examples/price_trigger_lock`](https://github.com/calledAdo/lean-oracle-v2/tree/main/examples/price_trigger_lock)
(the contract) and
[`examples/price-trigger-ts`](https://github.com/calledAdo/lean-oracle-v2/tree/main/examples/price-trigger-ts)
(the script that drives it).

The lock holds CKB for a beneficiary until a price crosses a strike, like a limit order in miniature.
The owner can take the funds back at any time. Once the condition holds, anyone can release the funds
to the beneficiary.

## What the lock stores

The lock's `args` pin everything it trusts:

| Bytes | Field |
|---|---|
| 0..32 | Type hash of the feed cell it reads |
| 32..64 | Committee type hash the feed cell must be anchored to |
| 64..96 | Feed ID |
| 96..104 | Strike price (i64, little endian) |
| 104..108 | Strike exponent (i32) |
| 108 | Direction: 0 = release at or above, 1 = at or below |
| 109..141 | Owner lock hash |
| 141..173 | Beneficiary lock hash |

## The contract

The release path reads the feed cell from the cell deps and checks it with the consumer helpers:

```rust
use lean_oracle_common::consumer::{check_feed_cell, price_at_expo, published_after};
use lean_oracle_common::publisher_set::PublisherSetData;

// 1. The pinned feed cell: right feed, right committee, a verified price the committee still backs.
let index = QueryIter::new(load_cell_type_hash, Source::CellDep)
    .position(|hash| hash == Some(args.feed_type_hash))
    .ok_or(ERROR_FEED_DEP_MISSING)?;
let data = load_cell_data(index, Source::CellDep).map_err(|_| ERROR_FEED_DEP_MISSING)?;
// The committee cell is a cell dep too: a pause or a revoked key set must reach this price.
let committee_index = QueryIter::new(load_cell_type_hash, Source::CellDep)
    .position(|hash| hash == Some(args.committee))
    .ok_or(ERROR_COMMITTEE_DEP)?;
let committee = load_cell_data(committee_index, Source::CellDep)
    .ok()
    .and_then(|bytes| PublisherSetData::from_bytes(&bytes))
    .ok_or(ERROR_COMMITTEE_DEP)?;
let feed = check_feed_cell(&data, &args.feed_id, &args.committee, &committee).map_err(to_error)?;

// 2. Fresh enough: published after every locked cell was created. Scripts cannot read
//    the current time, so the block header of each input (a header dep) provides one.
let header = load_header(0, Source::GroupInput).map_err(|_| ERROR_HEADER_DEP_MISSING)?;
published_after(&feed, header.raw().timestamp().unpack()).map_err(|_| ERROR_PRICE_STALE)?;

// 3. Compare at the strike's exponent.
let price = price_at_expo(&feed, args.expo).ok_or(ERROR_PRICE_SCALE)?;
let met = if args.at_or_below { price <= args.strike } else { price >= args.strike };
```

The full script also checks every input and that the beneficiary receives the locked amount. Reading
and checking the price costs about 38,000 cycles. The signatures were already verified when the feed
cell was updated.

## The transactions

<Steps>
<Step>
**Lock the funds.** Create a cell with the lock above and the amount to release. The example uses a
strike 1% below the current price so that it triggers straight away.
</Step>
<Step>
**Update the feed cell.** Call `pullAndUpdate` once the mirror has a price published after the
lock's block.
</Step>
<Step>
**Release.** Any keeper builds a transaction that spends the locked cell. It adds the feed cell as a
cell dep and the locked cell's block as a header dep, and pays the beneficiary.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Run it on testnet

You need Docker (the contracts build in a pinned container), Node 20+ and a funded testnet key.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/calledAdo/lean-oracle-v2 && cd lean-oracle-v2
./scripts/build-contracts.sh
cd examples/price-trigger-ts && npm install
LEAN_KEY_FILE=/path/to/testnet.key node index.mjs
```

The first run deploys the lock code (about 28,700 CKB of storage) and a feed cell, and caches both.
Each run then locks 250 CKB, updates the feed cell and releases the funds, printing every
transaction hash.
